name: list_sessions
description:
Every game session, from the sessions file and published by the hunt designer.

Each with its phase (`scheduled`, `running` or `stopped`), its planned window (only for
display: the moderator starts and stops a session), how many teams play it, and a link
to its moderator screen in the web app.

SessionSummary.description: A game session, without its codes or coordinates.
SessionSummary.title: SessionSummary

name: start_hunt_design
description:
Start designing a hunt for an area and theme; it runs for minutes in the background.

It reads OpenStreetMap and calls the Claude API, costing up to $1 a run, and only one
design runs at a time. Poll the draft with `get_hunt_draft` until it is `ready`.

outputSchema.description: The new draft; follow it with `get_hunt_draft`.
outputSchema.title: DesignStarted

name: list_hunt_drafts
description: The newest 50 hunt drafts, newest first: status, area, theme, checkpoints and cost.

name: get_hunt_draft
description:
One hunt draft in full: checkpoints, route, problems, progress and cost.

With `wait_seconds`, returns as soon as the draft's status changes, or at the timeout.
A draft holds coordinates and scenes: the answers to its clues, for the organiser only.

BoundingBox.description: The area's extent, in decimal degrees.
BoundingBox.title: BoundingBox

DraftArea.description: The area the run resolved; `clipped` if it was cut down to the size limit.
DraftArea.title: DraftArea

DraftChallenge.description: What the photo must show (`scene`, the clue's answer) and the pose to strike.
DraftChallenge.title: DraftChallenge

DraftCheckpoint.description:
A proposed checkpoint, with why the agent picked it and the organiser's review.

`original` keeps the agent's version of every field the organiser edited, from the
first edit on, so the two can be compared.
DraftCheckpoint.title: DraftCheckpoint

DraftOriginal.description: The agent's text for each field the organiser edited; None where it wasn't edited.
DraftOriginal.title: DraftOriginal

DraftPlace.description: A real place from the map data: its OpenStreetMap id, name, kind and location.
DraftPlace.title: DraftPlace

DraftRequest.description: What the organiser asks the designer for.

area.description: Where the hunt is, e.g. `Chiswick, London`
area.title: Area

DraftRequest.title: DraftRequest

Problem.description: A rule the draft breaks; `position` is the checkpoint's, or None for the whole draft.
Problem.title: Problem

ProgressEntry.description: One step of the run, for the organiser to follow; `at` is UTC to the second.
ProgressEntry.title: ProgressEntry

PublishedOut.description: The session the draft became, and when.
PublishedOut.title: PublishedOut

RouteOut.description: Each checkpoint to the next, closing the loop back to the first, in metres.
RouteOut.title: RouteOut

RunOut.description: The run behind the draft and what it cost.
RunOut.title: RunOut

outputSchema.description: A draft in full. Organiser only: it holds coordinates and scenes.
outputSchema.title: DraftOut

name: edit_hunt_checkpoint
description:
Edit, accept or reject one checkpoint of a `ready` draft; returns it as saved.

Set `review` to `accepted` or `rejected`; only accepted checkpoints are published.
Edited text is held to the same rules as the designer's: a clue can't name its place.

CheckpointEdit.description: What the organiser changes about a checkpoint: at least one field.
CheckpointEdit.title: CheckpointEdit

DraftChallenge.description: What the photo must show (`scene`, the clue's answer) and the pose to strike.
DraftChallenge.title: DraftChallenge

DraftOriginal.description: The agent's text for each field the organiser edited; None where it wasn't edited.
DraftOriginal.title: DraftOriginal

DraftPlace.description: A real place from the map data: its OpenStreetMap id, name, kind and location.
DraftPlace.title: DraftPlace

outputSchema.description:
A proposed checkpoint, with why the agent picked it and the organiser's review.

`original` keeps the agent's version of every field the organiser edited, from the
first edit on, so the two can be compared.
outputSchema.title: DraftCheckpoint

name: publish_hunt
description:
Publish the draft's accepted checkpoints as a session, playable at once. Final.

The result holds the session's join codes and its moderator code. They are credentials:
give each to its holders only (a team's join code to that team, the moderator code to
the moderator) and never repeat them elsewhere. No other tool returns them.

PublishRequest.description: The session to make of the draft: its name, planned window and teams.
PublishRequest.title: PublishRequest

TeamCodeOut.description: A team and its join code.
TeamCodeOut.title: TeamCodeOut

outputSchema.description: The published session and its codes: credentials, for the organiser only.
outputSchema.title: PublicationOut

name: list_submissions
description:
A session's submissions, newest first, as compact rows. No photos.

`filter`: `needs_review` (the default) is every photo the referee couldn't decide and
nobody has ruled on; `failed` and `passed` go by the effective verdict (what scoring
uses, the moderator's ruling over the referee's verdict); `overridden` is every photo
the moderator ruled on; `all` is everything. Each row has the referee's verdict, the
latest ruling, the effective verdict and the codes of the checks that failed. Page with
`before`: pass the previous page's `next` until it is null. Read a photo's reasons with
`get_submission`; the organiser views the photo on the moderator screen.

before.description: A submission id: the page starts below
before.title: Before

CheckpointOut.description: The photo's checkpoint. `name` is null if it's no longer in the sessions file.
CheckpointOut.title: CheckpointOut

SubmissionRow.description: A submission, compactly. `verdict` is the referee's; `ruling` the moderator's latest.
SubmissionRow.title: SubmissionRow

outputSchema.description: A page of submissions, newest first; pass `next` as `before` for the next page.
outputSchema.title: SubmissionList

name: get_submission
description:
One submission: why the referee decided as it did, and every ruling on it. No photo.

The pose the team was given and the scene it should show; each check with its outcome,
confidence, the reason the team was told and the detail behind it; the referee's status
and error code; and every ruling, oldest first (the last is in force). It does not
include the referee's raw trace or prompt. The scene and the details are the answers to
the clues: for the organiser only.

CheckpointOut.description: The photo's checkpoint. `name` is null if it's no longer in the sessions file.
CheckpointOut.title: CheckpointOut

RefereeOut.description: How the referee's call went: with an `error-code` there are no reasons to read.
RefereeOut.title: RefereeOut

StoredCheckOut.description: A check that ran: what the player was told (`reason`), and why (`detail`).
StoredCheckOut.title: StoredCheckOut

outputSchema.description: A submission in full, but for the photo.
outputSchema.title: SubmissionRead

name: override_verdict
description:
Approve or reject a photo, whatever the referee decided. Reversible.

The referee's verdict is never changed: the ruling is recorded beside it, and scoring
follows the effective verdict (`approve` counts as a pass, `reject` as a fail). An
approval completes the photo's checkpoint, and a later `reject` doesn't take that
back: it changes the team's score, not its progress. Ruling again on the same photo
replaces the ruling (`replaced` is true); the earlier one stays in the record. Allowed
while the session runs and after it stops. The `note` is for the record: it is never
logged, but don't put anything in it that you wouldn't want the moderator to read.

outputSchema.description: The ruling as `POST …/ruling` answers it, and whether it replaced an earlier one.
outputSchema.title: OverrideResult

name: start_session
description:
Start a scheduled session now: players can join and submit photos from this moment.

The planned window is only for display: the session runs from when it starts to when it
stops. A session that is already running is left as it is (`changed` is false). A
stopped session can't be started again (`session_stopped`).

outputSchema.description:
The session clock, and whether this call changed it: `false` when the session was
already in the state asked for.
outputSchema.title: ClockResult

name: stop_session
description:
Finish a running session, for good. Confirm with the organiser first: it can't be undone.

Players can no longer join or submit photos, and the session can't be started again.
Photos still waiting for a ruling can be ruled on afterwards; results are final once
every one has been. A session that is already stopped is left as it is (`changed` is
false). One that never started can't be stopped (`session_not_started`).

outputSchema.description:
The session clock, and whether this call changed it: `false` when the session was
already in the state asked for.
outputSchema.title: ClockResult

name: session_overview
description:
The moderator's view of a session: its clock, how many photos wait for a ruling, every
team's standing and progress (to spot a team that is stuck), and the newest attempts to
play outside the session.

Names checkpoints, but shows no coordinates, clues, scenes, photos or codes.

BlockedOut.description: A team that tried to play outside the session.
BlockedOut.title: BlockedOut

CurrentOut.description: The checkpoint the team is on.
CurrentOut.title: CurrentOut

LastCompletedOut.description:
The team's most recent photo that completed a checkpoint: which one, its effective
verdict and its receive time.
LastCompletedOut.title: LastCompletedOut

SessionClock.description:
Where the session stands, with its planned window and the server's time.

`planned-start`/`planned-end` are the file's times, for display only. `server-time` lets
the app correct for a phone whose clock is off. Times are UTC to the second.
SessionClock.title: SessionClock

TeamOverviewOut.description:
A team's standing and progress. Score fields are `null` for a team that hasn't joined.

`points`, `in-review` and `place` are exactly what the team sees in its own state.
TeamOverviewOut.title: TeamOverviewOut

outputSchema.description:
The session clock, the photos to review, the teams (standings first) and the newest
blocked attempts.

`to-review` counts the session's `pending` photos the moderator hasn't ruled on yet.
outputSchema.title: OverviewOut
